details: Bitcoin dipped on September 8th, impacted by a reported exploit on the Liquid Network and increasing investor concerns over potential Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. Macro caution set the tone, despite recent positive inflows into spot Bitcoin ETFs.
title: Bitcoin Slides as Fed Hike Odds Pass 60% After Liquid Exploit

details: The total crypto market cap rose 17.6% to $2.70 trillion in September 2026, marking the strongest ETF month of the year, according to Binance Research. Bitcoin surged 24.8% in seven days, indicating a rates-driven rally intertwined with US Treasury policy and Federal Reserve actions.
title: Crypto Market Cap Jumps 17.6% in September Rates-Driven Rally

details: Bitmine Immersion Technologies added 28,086 Ethereum last week, increasing its treasury to 5.93 million ETH, valued at nearly $15 billion as of September 8, 2026. The company is nearing its goal of owning 5% of Ethereum's supply, with most tokens staked for rewards.
title: Bitmine's Ethereum Holdings Near $15 Billion After Latest ETH Buy

details: Fresh US-Iran military exchanges over the weekend have pushed oil prices up and dragged Bitcoin below $79,000. Markets are now pricing a 57% probability of a 25bp Fed rate hike at the upcoming September 15-16 meeting, reversing earlier sentiment.
title: Geopolitical Tensions & Fed Hike Fears Push Bitcoin Below $79K

details: The global crypto market cap decreased by 0.7% to $2.76 trillion over the past 24 hours. Total crypto liquidations reached $182 million, with long liquidations slightly higher than shorts, as Bitcoin and Ethereum saw slight declines.
title: Crypto Market Cap Falls 0.7%; $182M Liquidated in 24 Hours

details: Bitcoin rose 0.45% as oil prices topped $100 and equities dropped following Iran strikes. Some altcoins also saw significant gains, while the taker buy-sell volume ratio turned neutral and short positions unwound.
title: Bitcoin Climbs as Oil Tops $100, Equities Drop After Iran Strikes

details: Approximately 235 exahashes per second (EH/s) of Bitcoin mining capacity is currently idle. Improved miner economics due to August's Bitcoin rally could bring this sidelined power back online, potentially increasing network competition.
title: Nearly a Fifth of Bitcoin Mining Power Idle, Could Re-Enter Market
